title: Ethics and data journalism: adding a new dimension to the data journalism pyramid
content:
Here’s a version of the inverted pyramid of data journalism that shows ethical considerations at each stage, thanks to the research of Laurence Dierickx, Marilia Gehrke and Carl-Gustav Linden which I blogged about yesterday.

The research maps the stages of the pyramid of data journalism to different categories and ethical justifications.

I’ve also added some others.

Privacy, for example, is listed in the research in relation to compiling data, but it is also a (potentially bigger) concern in communication: for example you might choose to use a heatmap instead of a points map to avoid identifying individuals, so in my diagram I’ve included privacy in both.

I’ve also included mentioned uncertainty in communication, as this is a major issue in data visualisation and journalism more generally.

Verification is listed in the research in relation to the compile stage, but it might also be one of the reasons for combining data or putting it into context: both stages might involve checking data against a second source.

Cleaning also often involves checking for outliers that may have been misentered, and duplication

title: Are newsroom guidelines fit for purpose when it comes to data journalism?
content:
News organisations’ guidelines haven’t kept up with developments in data-driven journalism, they need to learn from practices in other fields — and principles need to be embedded in practice, according to new research on data journalism ethics.

Researchers Laurence Dierickx, Marilia Gehrke and Carl-Gustav Linden looked at dozens of European news organisations’ ethical codes to see how they relate to each stage of the Data Journalism Pyramid. They conclude that while ethical codes might talk in general about ethical principles, they rarely provide any guidance on how to apply those in practice when it comes to data-driven reporting.

Underpinning the research is the concept of ‘epistemic governance‘: the idea that an individual journalist is not solely responsible for the ethics of newsroom output.

This “governance perspective”, they write, “asks how ethical obligations become embedded in the procedural architecture of journalistic workflows, shifting ethics from values to be held to conditions to be built into practice”.
